title: W4 camera-elevation labels stale after the W5 puck pad bump (0.95 -> 1.15): 'pucks ~65° STEEPEST' contradicts the committed SPRITE_SPECS
location: assets/blender/README.md:46 (also docs/silhouette-spec.md:40, tools/gen_sprites.py:191 and module docstring :41-42)
evidence:
tools/gen_sprites.py:125-127 commit the new pads:
    "puck_1":   ("puck",  1.15, "tier_4",  None),
    "puck_2":   ("puck",  1.15, "tier_8",  None),
    "puck_3":   ("puck",  1.15, "tier_16", None),
but tools/gen_sprites.py:190-192 still says:
    """ORTHO camera, the MM top-down tilt. Elevation above horizontal =
    atan(9.9 / (0.35 + 4.5*pad)) — pad 0.95 (pucks) => ~65deg STEEP (nearest
    top-down); pad 1.95 (campus) => ~47deg SHALLOW (most oblique). Any camera
and assets/blender/README.md:46:
| Camera | ORTHO, elevation ~47–65° above horizontal (varies with the per-sprite pad — camera Y scales with pad, Z fixed: pucks ≈65° STEEPEST / nearest top-down, campus ≈47° SHALLOWEST / most oblique; measured from the aim geometry) — the roof carries the read, thin outline visible all around |
(docs/silhouette-spec.md:40 repeats the same 'pucks ≈65° STEEPEST' claim.) Evaluating the code's own formula atan(9.9/(0.35+4.5*pad)) at the committed pads: puck pad 1.15 -> 60.83deg; house pad 1.12 -> 61.43deg (the actual steepest); campus pad 1.95 -> 47.33deg. 65.0deg corresponds only to the OLD pad 0.95.
detail: Rule 4: 'W4 camera labels inverted (steepest/shallowest) — fix + verify. Both verified in the PR body.' The PR body's 'elevation 47.3° … 65.0° (pucks, steepest) verified against rotation_euler' describes the pre-bump pad; at committed pads pucks are ~60.8° and house is steepest (~61.4°). Doc-only — renders are unaffected (double-run proven byte-identical).
recommended_fix: Re-measure at the committed pads and update README:46, silhouette-spec.md §0, and both gen_sprites.py docstrings to the real range ~47–61° (house steepest ≈61.4°, pucks ≈60.8°, campus ≈47.3°).

title: Gate-7 'negative self-test' is vacuous — it never feeds the mutated order through the comparator, so a comparator regression passes CI unflagged
evidence:
tools/test_sprite_order.py:59-66:
    fail = False
    if so != of or jo != of:
        fail = True
    # negative self-test: the comparator must BITE on a drifted order (a
    # comparator regression must never pass CI unflagged — #79 r2 W4)
    mutated = list(of)
    mutated[-1], mutated[-2] = mutated[-2], mutated[-1]  # the r1 swap itself
    if mutated == of:
        print("FAIL: negative self-test — mutation did not drift (broken test)")
`of` ends [..., "small_biz", "campus"] — swapping two DISTINCT elements always produces a different list, so `mutated == of` is always False and this leg can never fail; `mutated` is never passed to the so/of/jo comparison, so the comparator itself is never exercised on a drifted order.
detail: Carried #79 r2 item 'W4 (gate-7 negative self-test)' claims 'a comparator regression must never pass CI unflagged', but a regression (e.g. comparing sorted() lists) would still pass gate 7 green. Contrast tools/test_sprite_foldin.py leg 1, which feeds bad inputs into bbox_violation and asserts rejection.
recommended_fix: Feed the mutated list through the real comparator: extract a compare(a, b, c) helper from main() and assert it FAILS on (mutated, of, jo) — mirroring the working negative legs in test_sprite_foldin.py.
